summary: Implemented PRD_PARALLEL_REVIEWERS slice B on the controller, contracts and server adapter. Contracts: reviewCompletion.schema.json 1.2.0 (node_id ^review(-[a-z0-9-]{1,32})?$), feature.schema.json 2.1.0 (optional reviewers list), contracts/projects reviewResult 1.4.0 (reviewers entries, reviewer tag on every finding, unanimous approval rules; runInputs unchanged at 1.3.0), examples, READMEs and both contract tests updated, JSON schemas regenerated with npm run contracts:export. Controller: workflow/prompts/review.md holds the built-in brief; review_prompt(runtime, patch, reviewer) appends the fixed blocks to any brief; sessions.py adds reviewer ids (plan_reviewers, review_node); prepare --reviewer <id>=<brief> pins plan.reviewers; launch.py validates feature 2.1.0 reviewers (unique, not a lane, not reserved, brief exists and non-empty) and keeps 2.0.0/1.0.0 files on the default reviewer. automatic.py launches every reviewer over the shared review-worktree, wait_reviews polls every receipt with per-reviewer deadlines, per-reviewer status files automatic-review-<id>.json plus the combined automatic-review.json (the default reviewer's own status is merged into the combined file so slice A file names are unchanged), _decide over the set (unanimous approval; any block, unresolved P0/P1, rejected file or expiry blocks at once), combined review.json with reviewers entries and reviewer-tagged unioned findings, every reviewer stopped after the decision with superseded statuses, independence check across workers and reviewers, print fallback one job per reviewer in parallel. interactive.py: per-reviewer session names, files, attach-one --node review-<id>, one Claude: reviewer <id> pane per reviewer in declared order each split right of the previous; resume rebinds receipts and a reviewer interrupted before its receipt goes to needs_reconciliation with nothing relaunched. pipeline.py: check_review validates the reviewers list and the reviewer tag, manual review --reviewer <id> --review-file stores <node>.imported.json and combines once every declared reviewer is imported, approve is refused until then. export_state.py 1.4.0 adds review.reviewers (id, transport, session id, verdict, findings, launched_at, accepted_at, status) and finding.reviewer; server/projects.ts accepts exports 1.0.0-1.4.0 and fills a one-entry reviewers list named review for older exports on the unchanged reviews/<attempt> route. Example briefs in features/project-workflows/reviewers/ (general.md, coverage.md) with a README note; RUNBOOK, CHEATSHEET, workflow/README and contract READMEs updated. Tests: every reviewer test in test_automatic runs with one and with two reviewers (native and print); ParallelReviewerScenarios covers two-approve, one-blocks, p1-anywhere, one-times-out, wrong-node, shared-identity and interrupted-launch; default-reviewer is asserted by the single-reviewer classes; manual-import and declared-reviewer prepare/launch validation live in test_lanes; test_interactive covers per-reviewer sessions and panes; test_export covers 1.4.0 entries; server/projects.test.ts covers a two-reviewer export and the legacy fill. Checks executed in this worktree (after npm ci to obtain the pinned dependencies; no new dependencies): workflow-unit (.venv python -m unittest discover -s workflow -t .): 195 tests OK; shared-contract (npm run test:contracts): 18 pass, 0 fail; backend-regression (npm run test:unit): 130 pass, 0 fail; backend-build (npm run build): exit 0; additionally npx tsx --test server/projects.test.ts: 35 pass, 0 fail. Not executed: the section 8 live smoke test, the panes (live) and viewer-two-reviewers scenarios, and any Playwright suite (UI-owned). Nothing committed.
open_assumptions: Only reviewResult moves to contract 1.4.0; runInputs keeps contract_version 1.3.0 because its shape is unchanged. The UI fixture tests/project-workflows/fixtures.ts still projects reviewResult as 1.3.0 without reviewers and must be updated by the UI worker (it compiles, since validators take unknown, but fails at runtime).
With several reviewers, review.json 'reviewer' and the served reviewer.session_id list every reviewer's session id comma-separated in declared order; reviewers[] is the per-reviewer record.

The default reviewer's per-reviewer status is merged into automatic-review.json (no automatic-review-review.json) so a feature without reviewers keeps exactly slice A's file names; declared reviewers get automatic-review-<id>.json beside the combined file.

Per-reviewer status vocabulary: pending, launching, running, accepted, blocked, superseded, succeeded, needs_reconciliation; a deadline is recorded as blocked with a 'deadline exhausted' error, and the export maps statuses to accepted/blocked/superseded/pending (no separate expired value).

review.json is written on a deadline or rejected file only when at least one other reviewer's verdict was already accepted (retaining it, verdict blocked); with no accepted verdict no review.json is written, as before; identity, worktree or evidence refusals never record a partial review.
Reviewer id 'review' is reserved for the implicit default and cannot be declared in feature.json; declared reviewers always own review-<id>.
Manual mode: review without --reviewer is accepted only for a run with the single default reviewer; imports are stored as <node>.imported.json and each imported file must itself be approved.

interrupted-launch: on resume the reviewers that were launched are rebound and left running (not stopped) and the run stays at needs_reconciliation; the operator stops them by id and starts a new run.
features/parallel-reviewers/ was not touched (outside ownership); its own feature.json declares no reviewers, so this run's review uses the built-in reviewer.
